Fixed order: one regex such as foo.*bar; add rg/-w or rg/-F when you care about word boundaries or literal punctuation instead of regex syntax.

With rg/--pcre2, you can use lookaround; e.g. rg --pcre2 '(?=.*foo)(?=.*bar)' matches lines that contain both substrings (-P is the short form). Background: ripgrep FAQ — lookaround / backreferences.

File-level boolean/AND (each pattern appears somewhere in the same file)
How can I search for the boolean/AND of multiple terms in rg?

Run rg/--files-with-matches twice: list paths for the first term, then search only those paths for the second, e.g. rg -l --null 'foo' | xargs -0 rg -l 'bar' (rg/--null emits paths separated by ASCII/C0/NUL so xargs -0 survives spaces or odd characters). Intersecting two sorted rg -l lists with comm -12 is the same idea in another shape.

Using rg, how can I display + or - 8 lines of context around a match, plus line numbers?
Symmetric context (8 lines before and after each match): use -C 8 or --context=8, e.g. rg -n -C8 PATTERN path/. -C is shorthand for the same line count with -B and -A together.
Using rg, how can I display + or - 8 lines of context around a match, plus line numbers?

Asymmetric context (+8 after only / −8 before only): use -A 8 (--after-context=8) for lines after the match, or -B 8 (--before-context=8) for lines before. You can combine them independently, e.g. rg -n -B3 -A8 PATTERN (3 before, 8 after). Order matters when mixing with -C: later flags partially override earlier ones (see rg --help under -C).
Using rg, how can I display + or - 8 lines of context around a match, plus line numbers?
Line numbers: add -n or --line-number on the same command. Example with all three ideas: rg -n -C8 foo .

rga wraps rg to search inside file types ripgrep cannot read directly — PDFs, e-books, Office documents, zip/tar.gz archives, SQLite databases, and more — by transparently extracting text before matching.
Invoked as rga <pattern> <path>, mirroring rg usage; results and flags carry over from ripgrep.

The overall shape of the risks a tool, dependency, system, or decision carries: what can go wrong, how likely it is, and how much it would expose.
A profile is understood, not just measured — the goal is a mental model legible enough to reason about before committing.
Every choice to adopt a tool or design pattern imports its failure modes along with its benefits.
Comparing options is less about feature counts and more about which option's risk profile is easier to hold in your head and defend.
